clue.text: Squared up with a bank draft showing the account overdrawn

parts.note: a cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money
an overdrawn account is 'in the red', so red signals debt

explanation.surface: A bank statement settled up by cheque reveals the account was in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered pattern is marked out in squares like a draughtboard.

clue.text: Mount Clydesdale for instance

explanation.surface: Climb onto a big Scottish draught animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's mount is the steed carried on; a Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish breed of that animal.

clue.text: Share allocations for sound quoters

indicators.note: the clue says these words are to be heard, so their spoken form gives the entry

parts.note: people who quote, said aloud like the plural of a fixed share

explanation.surface: Portions are handed out to people who cite well.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed shares of a total assigned to each party are allocations.

clue.text: Make necessary use of home troops in the line up

indicators.note: the troops are placed within the turned word line
in a down clue, up means the word line is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force for home defence

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers are lined up for duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LINE into ENIL; 'in' puts TA within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To involve something as an unavoidable consequence is to require it.

clue.text: Hesitated in speech, then got it wrong

explanation.surface: Someone stammered and then made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as 'er-ed', saying 'er' while hesitating.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'er' while pausing is to have er-ed; to blunder or make a mistake is to have strayed from the truth.

clue.text: Lice cover as is reported to the welfare authority

indicators.note: read as re-ported, carried about again, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Infestation with lice has been notified to the welfare office.
explanation.definitionFit: State help for the needy is provided by the welfare department.

clue.text: Kind of lettuce suitable for sandwiches

explanation.surface: A soft-centred lettuce is just right in a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense describes a lettuce whose heart is soft enough to eat in a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kind is being compassionate; a lettuce with soft inner leaves has a tender heart.

clue.text: After teatime deb returns to see antique furniture

parts.note: four o'clock is the traditional British hour for afternoon tea
poster- is the Latin stem meaning coming after, as in posterior

indicators.note: the word deb is turned back to front

parts.note: a debutante, a young woman entering society

explanation.surface: A society girl comes back after tea to view some old furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with tall corner posts holding a canopy is a classic old piece of furniture.

clue.text: Tower of bell tents over a river in Egypt

parts.note: a group of bell tents makes an encampment
the Nile flows through Egypt

explanation.surface: A lookout overlooks a tented camp beside an Egyptian river.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian free-standing bell tower is the type of tower meant.

clue.text: Night-flare which can be carried with the greatest of ease

definitions.text: which can be carried with the greatest of ease

explanation.surface: A signal flare so weightless it is effortless to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol-fired signal flare is named after its inventor Very; anything extremely weightless is carried easily.

clue.text: Get up union demand

explanation.surface: Workers rise to press their claims.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as 'a rise', a pay increase a trade union demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand or rise from bed; a trade union's pay claim is for a raise.

clue.text: A trick to avoid

explanation.surface: A ruse for getting out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty ruse; to dodge is to evade or sidestep.

clue.text: New lamps for a song

indicators.note: new lamps are a fresh arrangement, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Echoes Aladdin's cry of new lamps for old, traded for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred hymn from the biblical book of praise songs.

clue.text: Pan robbed to pay Paul

explanation.surface: A pan is stolen to settle a debt with Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up shares his first name with the saint in the proverb about robbing one apostle to pay another.

clue.text: Skilful article written on cut-down of department

indicators.note: in a down clue, the article sits above the next piece

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
dept is the standard shortened form of department

explanation.surface: An expert writes a piece on an abbreviated government office.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly proficient means skilful.

clue.text: One who poses a challenge for the constructive hobbyist

definitions.text: a challenge for the constructive hobbyist

explanation.surface: A sitter presents a puzzle to someone keen on building kits.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's sitter strikes poses; a scale kit is something hobbyists build.

clue.text: Courteous East European invests it

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A Polish businessman puts money into something.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-mannered and courteous are synonyms.

clue.text: A bird that goes for outsize prey

parts.note: OS is the clothing-label abbreviation for outsize
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird of prey that targets large victims.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish hawk, a raptor that dives for fish, is a bird.

clue.text: Walk which is tiring in America?

explanation.surface: An exhausting American hike.
explanation.walkthrough: In American spelling a tyre is a 'tire', and its grooved surface is the tread.
explanation.definitionFit: To step or walk; the grooved rubber on a tyre (US 'tire').

clue.text: Require the French to construct a sewer

parts.note: to require is to need
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French drains needed to be built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' is one who sews, not a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tool used for stitching does the sewing.

clue.text: Young Greeks and Hebrews taken in by minced pie

indicators.note: one piece is swallowed inside the other
minced meat is chopped up, so the letters of pie are jumbled

parts.note: Heb is the abbreviation for the book of Hebrews

explanation.surface: Greek and Jewish youths are fooled by a mince pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minced' turns PIE into EPI; HEB goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece, youths entering manhood formed a class of young men.

clue.text: Gluttonous animal later regurgitated

indicators.note: brought back up, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A greedy beast throws up its food afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger, notorious for its greed, is this African mammal.

clue.text: How chess pieces are sold, whatever one possesses

explanation.surface: Chessmen are marketed and form all one's property.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as 'as sets', the way chessmen are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessmen come in complete sets; belongings of value are one's property.

clue.text: Come out from the merger

indicators.note: the entry is taken from inside the letters of the merger

explanation.surface: Something appears out of a corporate merger.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view or surface is to appear.

clue.text: One who courts the 50 and above

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
over means above

explanation.surface: Someone woos people aged fifty and older.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor who woos is a romantic partner.

clue.text: It flows through Russia and out of the country

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Russia
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia

explanation.surface: A river runs through Russia and out into the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to farmland and villages rather than towns.

clue.text: If you are to catch it the rod must be equal to it

definitions.text: If you are to catch it the rod must be equal to it

parts.words: If you are to catch it the rod must be equal to it
parts.note: a freshwater fish caught with rod and line, and also an old measure of length equal to a rod or pole

explanation.surface: An angler's rod must be up to landing the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater fish shares its name with a unit of length equal to the rod, five and a half yards.

clue.text: Where in Kent a writer for example turned up

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards

explanation.surface: An author turned up somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns EG into GE. Penge is a district of south-east London, historically in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A south London suburb that formerly lay in the county of Kent.

clue.text: A red carpet cannot be laid out by those who haven't got a bean

parts.note: scarlet is a bright red
a runner is a long narrow carpet

explanation.surface: The penniless can't afford to roll out the red carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haven't got a bean' is British slang for being broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant grown for its edible pods with red flowers is a type of bean.

clue.text: Famous 19th century surgeon in bed-with sunburn?

indicators.note: the surgeon is placed within the other word

parts.note: taken as written
Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery in the 1800s

explanation.surface: A Victorian surgeon is laid up in bed with sunburn.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly burnt skin rises in fluid-filled bubbles.
